summary: Asks the community to share which socket numbers their standard service programs use. For example, loggers listen on socket 1. It suggests assigning socket 5 for the mail-box protocol of RFC 196 and asks whether some sockets should be reserved for future standard services.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo asks which socket numbers standard service programs use on different hosts. It raises a possible socket number for a mail-box protocol and asks how future assignments should be handled.

questions: which sockets were used for standard services
how were well-known sockets assigned in 1971
what was socket 1 used for in 1971
what socket was proposed for the mail-box protocol
what does rfc 204 ask about socket numbers
subtitle: A request for information about socket numbers used by standard service programs.

tldr.problem: The author wanted to learn which socket numbers hosts used for standard service programs and how those numbers should be assigned.
tldr.mechanism: The memo asks hosts to report their socket usage, raises socket 5 for a mail-box protocol and asks whether some numbers should be reserved.
tldr.outcome: RFC 204 asks for comments by phone or mail and was updated by RFC 234.

today: RFC 204 was updated by RFC 234. Its status is listed as Unknown in the unit metadata.

sections.title: Collecting Socket Usage
sections.content: Jon Postel asks for information about the socket numbers used by standard service programs. He gives Loggers, or Telnet servers, listening on socket 1 as an example, and asks which sockets at each host are listened to by which programs.
sections.plainLanguage: The author wants a list showing which socket number each standard program listens on at each host.

sections.title: A Possible Mail-Box Assignment
sections.content: Dick Watson suggested assigning socket 5 to a mail-box protocol described in RFC 196. Postel asks whether anyone objects. He also asks for suggestions on how to assign sockets to standard programs and whether a subset should be reserved for future standard protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo asks whether socket 5 should be used for a mail-box protocol and whether some socket numbers should be set aside for future services.

sections.title: Request for Replies
sections.content: The memo asks readers to send answers and comments to Jon Postel by phone or mail. It proposes no final assignment rule in the text.
sections.plainLanguage: This note asks for information and opinions. It does not settle the socket-assignment questions.

references.text: RFC 196, mail-box protocol referenced in the socket 5 suggestion.
